I love Sweepy and it has absolutely become a crucial part of my cleaning and care routine! Sweepy helps me with two main things- keeping track of the last time I completed a cleaning or care task, and motivating me to complete those tasks. I use this app every day and I love it! That being said, there is room for improvement, and I hope this app keeps getting better and better.  I am so motivated by earning coins to buy furniture for my virtual house, but I wish there was a way to see all furniture available in the game. To clarify, I love that only a few items are available for purchase each day, and that the assortment changes each morning- it makes me want to run around getting things done when I see a special item in the store! However, I would really enjoy being able to see all the items (and the colors they come in) that *might* pop into the store so that I can choose favorite items to save up for. Perhaps there could even be a wishlist feature, and notifications for when a “wished for” item was on sale in the store, prompting users to open their app and get things done.  Another change I would like to see would be a way to see my whole house and rooms without having to click on them individually. As mentioned, collecting coins for furniture really works to motivate me, but it’s a bummer that the rooms are only visible when clicking on your to do lists. I would love if there was a dollhouse-style layout wherein I could click on the individual rooms to be transported to them and their tasks, making beautifying the virtual home more important as I’d see it right when I logged on. I’d also enjoy a bit more freedom when it came to using my furniture. For instance, Why can I only have one toy in the child’s room? Why can’t I put a plant in the bathroom? If I’m not using the default living room floor, why can’t I use it in my bedroom? Why do some items display as different sizes depending on where they are placed?  Maybe this is a premium feature, but I would really like to see the history of a task. Knowing the last time I completed a task is very helpful to me, but for some tasks, I need to keep track of more than just the most recent date it was completed. I’ve been using the very helpful “note” feature to just write down the last date before it is replaced by the “new” last date, but I worry that if I forget to do so, I cannot keep track of the history. Similarly, I am disappointed that there is no way to turn an “on demand” task into a recurring task. I can edit everything about the task, but I cannot add a recurring time period to a task that did not initially have one. Because of this, I’ve had to delete and re-add a few tasks that I had initially added as “on demand” when they felt too difficult to keep up with regularly, then wanted to make them recurring once I was ready for the challenge.   Lastly, I’d like to mention that as someone with ADHD who has trouble keeping up with a wide variety of repetitive care tasks that aren’t just cleaning related, I have several “rooms” in my “house” that are actually related to things like health, hygiene, or pets. Because Sweepy enables me to name each room whatever I want to, I am able to easily keep track of what tasks are where, even if it was not the virtual room’s intended purpose. Plus, it allows me, an apartment dweller with roommates, to decorate rooms I would not have otherwise had in my “house.” To name a few examples, I use the “Child’s Room” for tasks related to the care of my cat, the “Dressing Room” for beauty tasks like dyeing my hair or tracking my weight, and the “Office” for administrative tasks. With the ability to fully customize room names and task names and the large variety of available room types, I am perfectly content to use my virtual house in this way, but I felt I should mention it in case you are ever looking for ways to expand the game. Users could save coins to buy favorite food items to display in a “fridge” where tasks related to grocery shopping and food prep are kept, or animals, pet toys,  and pet beds could be purchased to display in a pet-care-centric area such as a Catio, Doghouse, or Stable.  Thanks for a great app!

First of all, I absolutely love this app!  It is, conceptually, exactly what I was looking for!   Unfortunately, I feel it doesn’t quite deliver in a way that keeps my ADHD brain (or the brains of my neurodiverse kiddos) engaged.  (I should note here that I am also physically disabled, and standing for any period of time, let alone cleaning, is challenging some days. Which makes this app both extra helpful, and at times extra frustrating).   It is just a little unbalanced for one. The most you can get for a task, no matter how laborious or gross, is 3 coins.  Items that come through the store often cost 30-65 coins. Nothing costs less than 5.  Sometimes cleaning takes me literal days to recover from. So there are days I will clean until my body physically can’t do on anymore (or anything else for the next few days), and realizing I’ve only earned less than half the cost of a refrigerator.  Even if I write down every last minor detail of the cleaning and set it to max difficulty/reward.  This is not exactly inspiring.   The store changes every day, which means you can’t really work towards a goal piece of furniture for your room either.   The placement of furniture and wallpaper is clunky at best. Positioning is fixed to certain spots in certain rooms, which is ok, but if an item is already in use there is no indication until you try to place it in the room you are decorating.  Then you have the option of removing it from wherever it is to place it, but there is no preview of what it would look like or way to undo that decision, meaning you have to backtrack and find where it was and put it back if you don’t like how it looks.   Objects change size from room to room (and slot to slot) but you cannot choose to resize an item. Making many items much less versatile or attractive than they could be.   All the rooms come with default furniture, walls, and floors, but those aren’t “real” items and can’t be moved from room to room (which if the rest wasn’t a pain wouldn’t matter, but it really does).   The store only sells one of each item displayed each day, even for common wallpaper and floors. Meaning if you want the same flooring in multiple rooms it will take forever and some good luck. This feels very silly.   What the game lacks most of all is a sense of reward agency. This is, in many ways, a self motivation app.  But I can’t configure the app to be motivating for me personally, despite knowing what would help.  Even just the ability to dole out bonus coin as a household manager would be hugely helpful.   My kids only engaged for one day, saw there was no real reward for participating, and fell off entirely.   I still feel like it was money well spent, just as an organized to-do list.  And I’m trying to think of ways to compensate for the apps lack of rewards that will re-engage my kids. (Something that would really be wonderful as a chronically ill solo parent!)   Things I love!   1) The ability to create your house and organize tasks by room.   2) The fact you can choose between daily, one time, and on demand tasks to assign to a space.   3) The household management system! I love being able to add my kids, whether they have their own accounts or not! (Mine do have devices, but was impressed there was an option to add them either way!)  I love that I was able to extend my purchase to their accounts through Apple family sharing, thank you for that!  And I love that I can configure the wildcard system, as the default was immediately intimidating.   4) I LOVE LOVE LOVE the streak feature! That is always such a good motivator!  Though the reward for keeping your streak is not motivating enough to keep my kids engaged, unfortunately.  I appreciate all the hard work that has clearly been but into the very solid bones and foundation of this app!  All that I love aside, it is hard to stay engaged, and even harder to convince my kids to open the app.  But it really doesn’t feel like it needs to be this way. It would take so little to make it so much better.  So here are some ideas:   1) Let us configure our coin rewards as a part of household management.   2) Let each household member pin an item in their personal store, so we can save towards a goal.   3) Let all/most items go in all rooms and in all slots. What does it hurt if we put a toilet in the bedroom? It is incredibly limiting at the moment, and disappointing when you can’t put, say, a potted plant outside or some such.   With this maybe let household management assign who can rearrange which room/lock rooms if that is not already a feature (I haven’t checked).   4) Let us chose the size of items that come in multiple sizes. Why is this rug nice and big in the bed room, and then tiny in the dining room? Etc.   5) Either have a store that has basic item like common walls and floors always for sale in addition to the store, or let us buy more than one wall/floor at a time.   6) Streak rewards. It feels more like a punishment to not keep your streak than a reward to keep it, which is not ideal in an app that is already unbalanced coin to cost wise.  Would love to see a real reward for engaging daily! I think my kids would actually use the app if that were the case! (Coin that ramps up each day? A piece of furniture on day X? Maybe a ticket for the store that can buy you anything after a month or some such?)   If you want more people to engage with your app, the decorating aspect really needs to be improved.  If you took it more seriously, and got it working well, you could eventually run daily login events and such with unique themed rewards.   It’s a really great app, and has the potential to be so much better and even more popular!   As it is, I intend to keep using it, or trying to, but I know I will fall off again most likely as it is largely an organized to-do list at the moment.  All the best, and thanks again for your hard work! I hope to see your app growing in popularity and success in the future!

Update: It seems as though the devs have taken my suggestion and implemented it in a way with personalized lists of tasks you select. I’m not a huge fan of the way they did it with a timer and pausing/resetting. Just a simple list would’ve been fine. But it functions the same way I suppose. Unfortunately, even though this app would now be a 5-star due to doing most all that I require…the app is often broken. I open it and sometimes only get a black screen. Not sure what the issue is all of a sudden, but now and then I have this issue. Eventually it works, but it is quite annoying. Original: I love that now my husband and I are keeping track our cleaning chores and when they need to be done. Used to be we wouldn’t clean unless something was really nasty and needed cleaned, which left our house always looking gross and our guests probably grossed out. Not anymore! Though there is about an hour’s-worth of initial setup required, the way the chores are structured, the entire house will eventually be cleaned, but since each piece is staggered, you won’t feel overwhelmed. Just a few chores one day, a few the next. I do have a few gripes/suggestions however. One is minor: there are chores such as “dust (quick)” and “dust (thorough)”. If you decide you want to do both, you had best add them to your list at the same time and stay on top of their due dates in order for them to be synchronized. I wish there was some way to have them synchronize automatically if they are both on the list. Not great for an ADHD family. I wish that if it’s going to autopopulate incorrectly, it wouldn’t autopopulate at all.
